elements.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Rendered § 20(h): "This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of New York." The prior Nova Scotia/Canada choice of law is fully displaced, with no residual reference to Canadian law elsewhere in the sentence.

elements.element: State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
elements.evidence: Rendered § 20(h) second sentence: "All disputes under this Agreement shall be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County." Both state and federal courts are named, the venue is New York County, and "non-exclusive" is replaced by "exclusive." No alternate merits forum or arbitration seat is retained; the absence of a temporary-injunctive-relief carve-out is permissive, not a defect, since the element only tolerates such a carve-out rather than requiring it.

elements.element: The governing law is Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause selects the laws of the State of New York, not Delaware, California, or England and Wales. This is expected because the drafter targeted the preferred level, which is superior for us.

elements.element: The dispute forum is the corresponding Delaware or California courts, or the courts of London for England and Wales law.
elements.evidence: The forum is the state and federal courts in New York County, not Delaware/California courts or the courts of London. Again a consequence of targeting the preferred level.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: both preferred elements are met in operative language (New York governing law; exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County). The fallback level is unmet only because the preferred, more favourable position was taken.

Underlying classification of deviation is correct: original § 20(h) chose Nova Scotia law (Vendor's home jurisdiction, outside the accepted set) and, worse, only non-exclusive Nova Scotia jurisdiction, failing the fallback on both law and forum. No arbitration clause exists, so this is deviation rather than walk-away.

Minimal: the edit replaces only the jurisdiction words and the forum words, preserving the two-sentence structure and the surrounding phrasing ("This Agreement shall be governed by...", "All disputes under this Agreement shall be subject to..."). Deletion of "and the laws of Canada applicable in Nova Scotia" is necessary, not cosmetic, because leaving it would create a contradictory second governing law. No survival tails, procedures, fee-shifting, service-of-process or waiver-of-inconvenient-forum boilerplate were added.

Preserves intent: the change from non-exclusive to exclusive jurisdiction is within the redline guidance (the preferred element expressly requires exclusivity over the merits) and does not disturb any other allocation, remedy, timing or cross-reference. The indemnity's reference to arbitration fees at p0090 remains a cost-category reference only and is not contradicted, since no arbitration agreement is created or removed.

No repair required. Optional (not a defect): if Vendor pushes back, we could add the customary "except that either party may seek temporary injunctive relief in any court of competent jurisdiction" carve-out, which the preferred element tolerates, or fall back to Delaware, California, or England and Wales with London courts as flagged in the margin comment.
